Q: When to use `--attach` with `docker container run`? A:

If you do not specify -a then Docker will attach to both stdout and stderr when running in foreground mode. You can use --attach option to attach to specific streams instead. 

-a=[]           : Attach to `STDIN`, `STDOUT` and/or `STDERR`

docker run -a stdin -a stdout -i -t ubuntu /bin/bash

Q: Is YouTube Data API v3 channel ID unique? A:

This is implied by ID it's used to uniquely identify a record.

So, to answer your question:

  1. One ID can only identify one record, so No, 2 channels can never have the same channel ID.

  2. Yes, the channel ID is permanent and immutable, the user might change their handle or username, but the ID remains the same.

  3. No, The IDs aren't "recycled" for new users

Q: Framer Motion not updating scrollYProgress A: 
Framer Motion useScroll never updates when using a custom scroll container in Next.js

I was trying to animate a section in my Next.js app using Framer Motion's useScroll:

const { scrollYProgress } = useScroll({
  target: containerRef,
  offset: ["start start", "end start"],
})

useMotionValueEvent(scrollYProgress, "change", (v) => {
  console.log("Scroll progress:", v)
})

…but scrollYProgress never changed, and the onChange callback never fired. Even logging window.scrollY showed 0 while scrolling the page.

What I found

After debugging:

  1. My globals.css had:
html,
body,
#app {
  height: 100%;
  max-width: 100%;
  overflow-x: hidden;
}

  • This meant the page height was fixed to the viewport.

  • All vertical scrolling happened inside a child container, not window.

  1. Framer Motion's useScroll defaults to window if no container is specified.

  • Since window.scrollY never changed, scrollYProgress stayed at 0.

  • Even correct offsets and a valid containerRef for the target didn’t help.

    The solution

    I needed to remove height:100% or explicitly tell useScroll which element is actually scrolling.

Q: Updating jar manifest file - java.io.IOException: invalid manifest format A:

I got the same error: java.io.IOException: invalid manifest format. In my case the cause was weird. Somehow a copy of WEB-INF and META-INF folders got copied to my WEB-INF/classes folder in my IDE and ended up in the war file. The unwelcomed and unexpected WEB-INF/classes/META-INF folder had an invaid MANIFEST.MF file. That took me a while to figure out because the /META-INF/MANIFEST.MF file in the right place was perfectly valid. Nothing wrong with it. I just had some extra files and folders that did not belong in the classes folder. The solution for me was to just delete the extra out-of-place WEB-INF and META-INF folders.
